questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: The first endocrine organ to form is the ___, beginning at about ___ weeks of gestation.
questions.exp: The source calls the thyroid the first endocrine organ formed, at 3–4 weeks. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: Match the following developmental steps — 1) Germ layer 2) Initial site 3) Destination of descent … A) Endoderm B) Anterior to trachea C) Floor of primitive pharynx
questions.exp: The follicular thyroid arises from endoderm in the primitive pharyngeal floor, descends anterior to the trachea and forms lobes. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: A midline subhyoid neck swelling moves on swallowing and tongue protrusion. Which embryologic remnant is most likely?
questions.exp: The chapter pairs thyroglossal cyst with midline subhyoid position and movement on deglutition and tongue protrusion. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: In the source's simplified 'after 5 weeks' branch, persistence is linked to a cyst and the tongue remnant is the ___.
questions.exp: The diagram labels the foramen cecum as the remnant; the exact involution timeline is simplified, so do not equate its 5-week heading with a universal completion date. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: Which is the odd one out for a typical thyroglossal cyst in this chapter?
opts: Lateral swelling fixed during tongue protrusion
questions.exp: The source emphasizes subhyoid position and mobility with swallowing/tongue protrusion; a fixed lateral swelling suggests a different differential. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: An uncomplicated thyroglossal cyst is treated by simple incision, then develops persistent drainage. Which complication and preferred operation match the source?
opts: Fistula; Sistrunk excision with central hyoid segment
questions.exp: The diagram warns that incision can produce a fistula and favors excision with the hyoid component by Sistrunk operation. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: Assess: I The thyroid pseudocapsule is derived from pretracheal fascia. II Berry ligament is described here as a condensation of the carotid sheath.
questions.exp: The source links the pseudocapsule to pretracheal fascia and describes Berry's ligament as its posterior condensation attached to the cricoid region. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: Match the following vascular origins — 1) Superior thyroid artery 2) Inferior thyroid artery 3) Thyrocervical trunk … A) Thyrocervical trunk B) External carotid C) Branch of subclavian system
questions.exp: The diagram traces superior thyroid supply from the external carotid and inferior thyroid supply through the thyrocervical trunk of the subclavian system. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: A surgeon dissects the superior thyroid vascular pedicle near a nerve supplying the cricothyroid. Which nerve is at risk?
opts: Internal branch of superior laryngeal nerve
External branch of superior laryngeal nerve
questions.exp: The vascular figure highlights the external superior laryngeal branch near the superior thyroid artery; the internal branch has a different course. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: The laryngeal nerve labeled near the inferior thyroid artery is the ___ nerve.
questions.exp: The inferior thyroid artery–recurrent laryngeal nerve relationship is a key surgical relation in the diagram. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: For the neck illustration, evaluate: I Superior and recurrent laryngeal nerves are branches of the vagus. II The common and external carotid arteries are both labeled in the arterial tree.
questions.exp: The diagram labels vagus, superior laryngeal branches, bilateral recurrent nerves and the carotid arterial system. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: The radiographic caption shows a cyst below the hyoid. Which anatomical descriptor should be used?
questions.exp: The image is explicitly labeled thyroglossal cyst in the common subhyoid position. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
questions.q: Assess thyroglossal cyst origin: I It is a congenital developmental remnant. II Congenital origin establishes a Mendelian inheritance pattern.
questions.exp: Thyroglossal cysts arise from developmental duct persistence; congenital does not imply a defined inherited Mendelian syndrome. (Book p898)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: The structural and functional thyroid unit is the ___, with ___ in its lumen.
questions.exp: The figure shows follicular epithelial cells surrounding colloid; the follicle is the functional and structural unit. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Match the following source developmental milestones — 1) Thyroglobulin appearance 2) Hormone synthesis begins 3) Initial gland formation … A) 29th day B) 11th week C) 3rd–4th week
questions.exp: The page gives thyroglobulin by day 29 and synthesis by week 11; initial gland formation is earlier in the chapter. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Assess: I Parafollicular cells supply the main thyroglobulin-derived T3/T4 pool. II Thyroglobulin is a hormone precursor in the follicular system.
questions.exp: Follicular cells make thyroglobulin and thyroid hormones; parafollicular C cells instead secrete calcitonin. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Parafollicular C cells secrete ___ rather than T3 and T4.
questions.exp: The C-cell note specifically identifies calcitonin secretion. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: A student uses this page's classical embryology scheme to trace parafollicular cells. Which association matches that scheme?
opts: Ultimobranchial body and caudal pharyngeal-pouch complex
First pharyngeal arch and Meckel cartilage
Dorsal pancreatic bud and neural tube
questions.exp: The source describes ultimobranchial/neural-crest and partial fifth-pouch origin. This is a classical teaching model; modern mammalian lineage evidence supports endodermal C-cell origins rather than an unqualified neural-crest claim. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Match the following regulatory levels — 1) Hypothalamus 2) Pituitary 3) Thyroid follicle … A) T3/T4 B) TRH C) TSH
questions.exp: The positive axis is hypothalamic TRH → pituitary TSH → thyroid T3/T4 production. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: A patient with hypopituitarism has low free T4 and a TSH within the laboratory range. Which interpretation is best?
opts: Normal thyroid function maintained by basal synthesis
Primary thyrotoxicosis with pituitary TSH suppression
Central hypothyroidism with an inappropriately normal TSH
Primary hypothyroidism with an appropriate TSH response
questions.exp: A source claim about basal synthesis does not exclude central hypothyroidism. Low or inappropriately normal TSH with low free T4 requires evaluation. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Match the following developmental factors — 1) TTF-1 2) PAX8 3) PROP1 … A) Choreoathetosis association B) Congenital hypothyroidism C) Combined pituitary hormone deficiency
questions.exp: The table pairs TTF-1 with choreoathetosis, PAX8 with congenital hypothyroidism and PROP1 with combined pituitary deficiency. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Congenital hypothyroidism is accompanied by a developmental cleft abnormality in the source table. Which factor is implicated?
questions.exp: TTF-2 is linked to thyroid dysgenesis and a cleft entry. The page says 'cleft thyroid'; the recognized FOXE1-associated syndrome includes cleft palate, so the literal label is imprecise. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: A child with congenital thyroid dysfunction also has choreoathetotic movements. Which developmental gene association is most relevant?
questions.exp: The TTF-1 row highlights choreoathetosis; it is distinct from the PAX8 and pituitary PROP1 associations. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Which is the odd one out for a primary thyroid-development factor in this table?
questions.exp: PROP1 is paired with combined pituitary hormone deficiency, unlike the thyroid-development entries. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
questions.q: Evaluate the final dysgenesis note: I Thyroid dysgenesis can cause congenital hypothyroidism. II Most cases must be proven TTF-1 or TTF-2 mutations because those factors are named.
questions.exp: The source links these factors to dysgenesis but its causal/frequency wording is confused. Naming genes does not establish that they explain most cases of congenital hypothyroidism. (Book p899)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Match the following membrane events — 1) Basolateral iodide entry 2) Apical iodide movement 3) TSH signal … A) Cl–I exchange by pendrin B) Na–I symport C) cAMP increase
questions.exp: The schematic places NIS basolaterally, pendrin at the apical iodide pathway and TSH receptor signaling through cAMP. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: The immediate second-messenger rise shown after TSH receptor binding is ___.
questions.exp: The synthesis diagram labels increased cAMP below TSH receptor binding. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: A transport defect prevents entry of iodide from blood into the follicular cell. Which transporter is primarily affected?
questions.exp: NIS traps iodide across the basolateral membrane; pendrin acts later at the apical side. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Match the following synthetic components — 1) TPO 2) DUOX2 3) Thyroglobulin … A) Thyroid peroxidase B) Tyrosine-rich scaffold C) Hydrogen-peroxide-generating system
questions.exp: TPO drives oxidation/organification and coupling using oxidizing equivalents supplied by DUOX2; thyroglobulin provides tyrosyl residues. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: At the apical thyroid interface, which system is required for iodination of thyroglobulin tyrosyl residues?
opts: Type II deiodinase with reduced glutathione
questions.exp: Thyroid hormone organification requires TPO and hydrogen peroxide; the handwritten enzyme-independent label should not be learned as established physiology. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Coupling MIT with DIT yields ___, while DIT with DIT yields ___.
questions.exp: The diagram gives MIT + DIT = T3 and DIT + DIT = T4 during coupling on thyroglobulin. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: A synthetic defect leaves iodinated thyroglobulin available but prevents the coupling reaction. Which enzyme is most directly implicated?
questions.exp: TPO participates in coupling iodotyrosines as well as the earlier oxidation/organification chemistry. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Match the following ordered events — 1) Colloid uptake into follicular cell 2) Proteolysis 3) Peripheral conversion … A) Release from thyroglobulin B) Retrieval of stored iodinated protein C) T4 converted to active T3
questions.exp: The later diagram steps are uptake of stored thyroglobulin, proteolysis and release, followed by peripheral conversion of T4. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: The source labels T4:T3 as ___ in the follicular stored material and ___ at hormone release.
questions.exp: These are the two ratios printed at successive locations in the diagram; they are not interchangeable labels for a measured free-hormone serum ratio. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Evaluate iodide's acute effect in the release diagram: I An inhibitory arrow points from iodide to hormone release. II This means more iodide always increases immediate hormone release.
questions.exp: The diagram marks acute iodide inhibition of release; iodine effects vary with dose, timing and underlying thyroid disease. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Only a minority of circulating T3 is secreted directly by the thyroid. Which source distribution best explains the remainder?
questions.exp: The page assigns 80% to peripheral conversion and 20% to direct synthesis, emphasizing T4-to-T3 conversion. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among non-thyroid NIS-expressing tissues listed?
questions.exp: The source's 'silent' tissue list names salivary gland, breast and placenta. NIS expression does not imply thyroid-hormone production in these sites. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: A nodule has reduced radionuclide uptake. Which conclusion avoids the source's overly broad 'cold nodule (malignant)' label?
opts: Both benign and malignant nodules can be cold
Every cold nodule is a carcinoma
Every cold nodule is an autonomous toxic adenoma
questions.exp: Reduced NIS expression/uptake can occur in adenoma or carcinoma; a cold scan is not a histologic diagnosis of malignancy. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Match the following inhibitors and steps — 1) Perchlorate/thiocyanate 2) Acute excess iodide 3) TPO inhibition … A) Impaired organification/coupling B) Reduced release C) Reduced iodide trapping
questions.exp: Perchlorate and thiocyanate compete at iodide uptake; excess iodide acutely inhibits release; TPO inhibition affects organification and coupling. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Assess iodide-uptake blockers: I Perchlorate and thiocyanate inhibit NIS-mediated uptake. II Both are routine first-line treatments for every form of amiodarone thyrotoxicosis.
questions.exp: The pharmacologic uptake inhibition is useful to learn, but thiocyanate is not a routine treatment and perchlorate use is restricted by toxicity and setting. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: A child has goiter and sensorineural hearing loss with an autosomal-recessive apical iodide-transport defect. Which diagnosis fits?
questions.exp: Pendred syndrome involves pendrin, a chloride–iodide exchanger, with goiter and SNHL; the source spells it 'Pendrin syndrome.' (Book p900)

questions.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
questions.q: Pendred syndrome's inheritance pattern is ___, and the transporter exchanges ___ with iodide.
questions.exp: The source labels the pendrin defect AR and identifies Cl−/I− antiport, distinct from the sodium–iodide symporter. (Book p900)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Match the following source iodine entries — 1) Adult requirement 2) Pregnancy requirement 3) Daily urinary repletion entry … A) >100 µg B) 220 µg/day C) 150 µg/day
questions.exp: The source prints adult 150 µg/day, pregnancy 220 µg/day and daily urinary iodine >100 µg. Do not confuse this daily amount with population urinary iodine concentrations in µg/L. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: A nuclear-medicine note concerns thyroid radioablation for Graves disease. Which isotope is paired with that use on the page?
questions.exp: The source assigns I-131 to radioablation and I-125 to brachytherapy; these therapy notes should not be confused with all diagnostic scintigraphy protocols. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Assess the isotope note: I I-125 is paired with Graves radioablation. II Brachytherapy is a diagnostic thyroid-uptake scan.
questions.exp: Brachytherapy is localized radiation treatment, not a thyroid-uptake scan; the source heading groups unlike applications. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: The principal enzyme family responsible for peripheral T4-to-T3 conversion is the ___.
questions.exp: Deiodination activates T4 to T3 or inactivates hormone depending on the isoenzyme and ring involved. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Match the following deiodinase distributions — 1) Type I 2) Type II 3) Type III … A) Liver/kidney B) CNS/thyroid/pituitary C) Placenta/hemangioma
questions.exp: These are the site groups printed in the three-column table; type II is labeled most abundant by the source. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: A very large hemangioma is associated with accelerated thyroid-hormone inactivation. Which enzyme is the best match?
questions.exp: The type III column includes hemangioma and conversion of T4 to reverse T3, consistent with an inactivating pathway. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Match the following deiodinase functions — 1) Type I 2) Type II 3) Type III … A) Local T4 to T3 activation B) Reverse-T3 degradation C) T4 to reverse T3
questions.exp: The table emphasizes rT3 clearance for type I, T3 generation for type II and rT3 formation for type III. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: In the source's illness model, assess: I Reduced type-II activity is followed by type-III activation. II Type III is an activating T4-to-T3 enzyme.
questions.exp: The schematic depicts D2 inhibition followed by D3 activation, including a skeletal-muscle note; D3 inactivates rather than activates thyroid hormone. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Which is the odd one out among the deiodinase inhibitors listed?
questions.exp: PTU, amiodarone, steroids and propranolol are listed; methimazole's principal action is intrathyroidal TPO inhibition rather than peripheral conversion blockade. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Besides PTU, amiodarone and propranolol, the listed drug class reducing peripheral conversion is ___.
questions.exp: Steroids are the fourth entry in the deiodinase-inhibitor list. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: The table gives free fractions of T3 and T4 as approximately ___ and ___ respectively.
questions.exp: T3 has the greater free fraction in the source comparison; the decimal places matter. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Match the following T3/T4 properties — 1) T3 half-life 2) T4 half-life 3) Relative biological potency … A) About one day B) T3:T4 about 4:1 C) About one week
questions.exp: The table lists one day versus one week. Its row labeled 'Pathway' with values 4 and 1 is interpreted as relative potency, not four separate synthesis pathways. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: After several days of fasting during critical illness, a patient has low T3, high reverse T3, and initially normal T4 and TSH. Which pattern matches the source?
questions.exp: The early sick-euthyroid/low-T3 stage is T3 down, rT3 up and T4/TSH initially normal in the diagram. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Assess thyroid testing in critical illness: I ICU admission excludes coexisting intrinsic thyroid disease. II Thyroid testing remains appropriate when there is a specific clinical suspicion.
questions.exp: Non-thyroidal illness complicates interpretation; it does not prohibit testing for a genuine thyroid indication. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: In the source's middle-stage schematic, TSH and T3 ___, whereas reverse T3 and T4 ___.
questions.exp: That is the printed middle-stage pattern. The T4 rise is not a required universal trajectory; real non-thyroidal illness can have normal or low T4 depending on severity and context. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: Match the following source illness stages — 1) Early 2) Middle 3) Late … A) All four hormone entries fall B) TSH/T3 low, rT3/T4 high in this diagram C) T3 low/rT3 high, T4 and TSH initially normal
questions.exp: The three-stage chart ends in rapid catabolism with lower T4, TSH, rT3 and T3. It is a teaching schematic, not a mandatory sequence in every patient. (Book p901)

questions.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
questions.q: A critically ill patient's late-stage chart shows all measured thyroid-related hormones falling. Which explanation is printed at that stage?
questions.exp: The final branch labels rapid catabolism with falls in T4, TSH, rT3 and T3; clinical interpretation must still consider medications and genuine thyroid disease. (Book p901)

units.title: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants
units.sec: Thyroid embryology, surgical relations and thyroglossal remnants · p898
units.guide: Trace endodermal thyroid descent and thyroglossal persistence. Connect the arterial diagram to nearby laryngeal nerves. Distinguish the preferred Sistrunk excision from incision that risks a persistent fistula.

units.title: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors
units.sec: Follicles, C cells and developmental transcription factors · p899
units.guide: Separate follicular hormone synthesis from C-cell calcitonin secretion. Learn the timeline and transcription-factor associations while flagging the source’s overstatement that low TSH cannot cause significant hypothyroidism.

units.title: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects
units.sec: Thyroid hormone synthesis and transport defects · p900
units.guide: Follow basolateral trapping, apical iodide transport, TPO-dependent chemistry, colloid storage and proteolytic release. NIS and pendrin are different transporters; a cold nodule is not synonymous with malignancy.

units.title: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness
units.sec: Iodine, deiodinases and non-thyroidal illness · p901
units.guide: Learn the iodine entries, isotope applications, deiodinase sites and inhibitors, then T3/T4 properties. Distinguish the source’s staged sick-euthyroid schematic from a mandatory laboratory trajectory in every ICU patient.
